- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (true outcome > 2.5), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 15–30% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >2.5 and true outcome drops below 1.5, adjust downward by 20–40% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 0.00 or -0.33), model underestimates; apply upward bias of 15–25% for 1–3 day horizon.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment >0.67 for 5+ days, add 5–10% upward bias to 30d forecast.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) for 7+ days, model tends to overfit recent history; apply 10–15% downward correction to 30d forecast.
